_note: The Care engine's own contract: who may be offered which visit, in what order, what an offer does when nobody answers it, which protocols a visit's checklist runs under, and the sample visit the nurse workspace walks. packages/catalog/apis/care.json is the frozen shape of the routes and holds every refusal sentence a route answers with; this file holds the rules those routes are computed from, and points at a route's sentence rather than repeating it. packages/engines/src/care/domain reads it; scripts/emit-care.mjs writes it, with the route sentences it points at, into Swift and Kotlin.
_fiction: Nothing here dispatches anybody. The candidates are packages/catalog/roster.json's nine fictional nurses, the Trust Score badges are stood in for by the preview's own vetting arithmetic, and the sample visit is walked on one device with nobody at the other end of it.
_seedPhaseNote: A service in packages/catalog/services.json whose phase is later than this one is not offered to anybody. The phase lives in services.json and nowhere else; this is the line the engine reads it against.
_servicesNote: One row per service in packages/catalog/services.json, and the build fails on a service without one. A scope is one of the options the vetting register gives a nurse and a locum, or null where none of the seven names the work: an injection, family planning and a sick-note assessment are inside a registered nurse's general scope rather than a named one, and that reading is the programme's, awaiting the Clinical Governance Lead. Since 15 September 2026 those three rows name the setting that holds their roles (rolesFromSetting) instead of a list of their own: who may be offered them is an admin setting that waits on a clinical review, so the roles live in settings and nowhere else. Allied health and the home carer have no role on the vetting register, so nobody can be matched to either, and the carer row says who a carer would be supervised by so that the refusal is written before the role exists rather than after.
_protocolsNote: Ids from packages/catalog/protocols.json and nothing else. Family planning and the men's and mental-health check-ins have no protocol in the register; their checklist says so rather than borrowing a neighbour's.

settings._note: Care's settings, in the shape packages/catalog/settings.json gives every setting. How long an offer lasts moved here from offers on 15 September 2026, when the founder instructed that open questions become admin settings: the value, who proposed it and who decided it are unchanged, and an admin now changes it on the back office's Configuration tab within bounds that are themselves proposals. packages/engines/src/care reads the value in force when it makes an offer and keeps the expiry on the offer, so a change never reaches an offer already made. GET /v1/care/settings@1, POST /v1/care/setting-changes@1 and POST /v1/care/setting-reviews@1 answer through packages/engines/src/settings. The scope settings — who may be offered an injection, a family planning or a sick-note visit — and whether an Encounter entry counts as signed joined on 15 September 2026 as proposals by the integrator, each waiting on a clinical review by somebody who holds sign-clinical-review. Until a reviewer confirms the exact value in force it is in force and shown as not clinically reviewed; care is not stopped for it, because the value in force is today's behaviour and stopping those visits would take care away from patients over paperwork nobody has done yet.
settings.heading: Care settings
settings.intro: How long a nurse has to answer an offer, who may be offered the visits no named scope covers, and what Care accepts as a signed encounter until the record can say.

items.label: Offer expiry
items.help: How long a nurse has to answer an offer before it goes to the next nurse who is eligible for it.

default.why: An unanswered offer must not hold a patient's visit, which is the reason appointment.offered carries offerExpiresAt at all. Ten minutes is long enough for a nurse finishing a dressing to wash her hands and read it, and short enough that three nurses in a row not answering is half an hour rather than half a morning. The Care lead proposed it and the founder decided it on 15 September 2026 ("Care: 10min").

lowest.proposedBecause: Three minutes is about as quickly as a nurse can finish what her hands are doing, wash them and read an offer. Shorter, and offers lapse on nurses who were about to take them, and the visit goes down the list for nothing.

highest.proposedBecause: Three times the founder's ten. Past half an hour, three nurses in a row not answering holds a patient's visit for an hour and a half, which is a morning lost rather than a wait.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to offers made after it. An offer already made keeps the expiry it was made with, and lapses when it said it would.

guardrail.statement: An offer always lapses, and never holds a patient's visit for longer than half an hour. No value lets an unanswered offer keep a visit from the next nurse.

items.label: Who may be offered an injection visit
items.help: Which registered roles an injection visit may be offered to.

default.proposedBecause: It is exactly what Care does today: any registered nurse or locum. No scope on the vetting register names injections yet, so the programme reads them as inside a registered nurse's general scope, and that reading waits on a clinical reviewer.

allowedRoles.proposedBecause: The roles on the vetting register granted take-visit, which is what lets anybody attend a patient at home. A role without it could be named and never sent, which looks like a shortage rather than a mistake.

lowest.proposedBecause: A service offered in phase one is offered to somebody. Withdrawing a service is its phase in packages/catalog/services.json, not a role list naming nobody.

highest.proposedBecause: Every role that may attend a visit, and no more.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to offers made after it. An offer already made keeps the roles it was made under, and a visit already accepted stays with the nurse who accepted it.

guardrail.statement: Nobody the vetting register does not let attend a patient visit is ever offered an injection: never a carer, an operator, an admin or a courier, and never nobody.

items.label: An Encounter entry counts as signed
items.help: Whether Care treats an Encounter entry the record has written as a completed and signed encounter, until a record route can tell Care whether it was signed.

default.proposedBecause: There is no record route Care may call yet. passport.entry.written@1 for an Encounter is the only way Care learns an encounter exists, so today Care counts that entry as complete and signed, and switching it off would stop every handover and completion until a record route answers.

allowed.label: Counts as signed
allowed.proposedBecause: Today's behaviour, while no record route answers Care.

allowed.label: Wait for a record route
allowed.proposedBecause: For a reviewer who decides an entry written is not proof of a signature. Handover and completion are then refused until a record route answers Care.

items.appliesTo: A change applies to visits started after it. A visit already under way is handed over and completed under the value it started with, so a nurse at a door is never refused by a change made after she knocked.

changelog.why: The Care lead proposed ten minutes and the founder decided it: "Care: 10min".

The founder instructed that open questions become admin settings. Who may be offered the three visits no named scope covers, and whether an Encounter entry counts as signed, were questions for the Clinical Governance Lead; each is now a setting whose default is what Care already did, waiting on a clinical review.

offers._expiryNote: How long an offer lasts is the setting offer-expiry in settings above: decided by the founder, changed by an admin within its bounds, and read by the engine when it makes an offer. Nothing in this block holds it.

order.why: A patient who names a nurse is asking for the person she already trusts in her house. She is asked first, if every gate lets her be asked at all.

order.marker: You have seen this patient before
order.why: Continuity is clinical before it is courtesy: a nurse who dressed a wound last week can see whether it is better. The most recent nurse is asked first.
Everybody else, nearest first, by the straight line between two suburb centres in packages/geo. Not a driving time, and the offer card says so.

offers.declined: It has gone to the next nurse who is eligible for it.
offers.lapsed: Nobody answered in time, so it went to the next nurse who is eligible for it.

withheldIsNotLast.statement: A nurse who fails a gate is withheld, not ranked last. She is not on the list at all, and the reason is said.
withheldIsNotLast.why: A list ordered with the ineligible at the bottom is a list somebody works down to the bottom of on a busy morning. Withholding is the only arrangement in which a failed gate cannot be reached by patience.

withheld.statement: Nobody is offered a visit from a place the map cannot measure a distance from.
withheld.why: Three of the roster's nurses work where packages/catalog/geography.json has no suburb. A distance invented for them would rank them against people whose distance is real.

position.whileShared: Today, until this visit is complete, this patient is shown the suburb you are in. Never a street, and nothing after the visit ends.
position.why: packages/catalog/geography.json already refuses a patient a street-level position and anything before the day. Care adds the other end: the visit's completion is when the sharing stops, not the end of the nurse's shift.

checklist.noProtocol: No protocol in the register covers this service, so there is no checklist to run.

record.sentence: The readings and your sign-off are the visit assessment. This visit is handed over and completed against what it seals, and against nothing typed here.

handover.queued: Handed to the doctors' review queue.

complete.billable: The visit is complete. Money is told it is billable and is told nothing about what happened at it.

sync.whyOnlyCapture: A reading taken with no signal is the one piece of a visit that has to be allowed to arrive late. A start, a handover and a completion each ask something of somebody at the time — the code from the patient, a complete encounter from the record — and replaying one from a queue an hour later would be answering that question on the patient's behalf.

preview.why: The one visit the nurse workspace walks. Sister Naledi Mokoena dressed this patient's wound before, so continuity puts her first if every gate lets her be asked; the order is computed from the roster, not chosen here. The code is the preview's published one, printed on the screen so the preview can be walked; a real visit code is issued to the patient and never written anywhere a nurse can read it.
